docs.text:
From How Strider Set Goal, Start Navigation (Strider) SSH workspace sodero tools call navigation.navigate_to_pose, navigation.get_status, navigation.cancel_navigation, localization.set_initial_pose Your module A module connected to the Navigator's navigation port; it can send goals and follow their progress (Create Custom Modules)

A goal is a pose in the map frame. A patrol is a sequence of goals sent one after another by your program.

docs.title: Navigate in Simulation
docs.text:
This tutorial continues the Quick Start. You add a camera, the Localizer and the Navigator to the simulated Jackal, load the map of its warehouse, let the robot find itself on the map, and send it to a goal.

The Jackal (center) driving to a goal in the warehouse, guided by the Station's navigation stack

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text: You need Details The Quick Start setup sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal and sodero.mlc.jackal, running, with the Jackal driving in Isaac Sim The example scene jackal_warehouse.usd from the Quick Start (jackal_warehouse.zip). The Jackal carries a depth camera cam0 on its base_link, 0.22 m ahead of the base and 0.47 m above the floor, looking forward with a 90° horizontal field of view. The map bundle warehouse.nav.tgz: the map of the warehouse scene with the settings used in this tutorial

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare Isaac Sim
docs.text:
The localizer in this tutorial uses the camera at 320 × 240 pixels and 5 frames per second. Isaac Bridge renders cameras at 640 × 480 and 15 frames per second unless told otherwise, so start Isaac Sim from its installation folder with this camera setting (close it first if it runs):

LinuxWindows (Command Prompt) 
RC_ISAAC_CAMERA_DEVICES='[{"name": "cam0", "width": 320, "height": 240, "fps": 5}]' ./isaac-sim.sh

set "RC_ISAAC_CAMERA_DEVICES=[{"name": "cam0", "width": 320, "height": 240, "fps": 5}]"
isaac-sim.bat

Then open jackal_warehouse.usd and press Play. The Isaac Bridge window lists cam0 320x240 at 5 fps.

Check two more things before you go on:

  • Clocks. The clocks of Stellar X and the Isaac Sim computer must agree within 20 ms. Synchronize both with a time server (NTP). If you cannot, see Camera Timing.
  • Quick Start nodes. If you restarted Isaac Sim for this step, restart the Quick Start nodes once the scene plays: Stop all nodes, then Start all nodes (Connect to Stellar Station › Stop, Pause and Play). Both nodes show Operating again.

docs.title: Step 2: Add the Camera Gateway
docs.text:
1. Add node › Gateway › Camera gateway, name it cam0 (Sensors and Cameras).
  2. In its inspector, set Camera name cam0 (the camera prim's name in the scene) and Camera host (the Isaac Sim computer). The port is 53335.
  3. Under CAMERA SETTINGS, set fps 5, frame id cam0_optical, intrinsics mode fov with a horizontal field of view of 90, and click Save settings.
  4. Click Start node, then Camera view on its card to check the image. If the image stays empty, see Camera Timing.
The Jackal's camera

docs.title: Step 3: Add the Localizer and Load the Map
docs.text:
1. Add node › Controller › Localizer. It is named sodero.localizer.
  2. In its inspector, click Upload .nav and choose warehouse.nav.tgz. The inspector shows the map: warehouse · 500×620 @ 0.05 m, and the initial pose of the bundle.
The localizer with its map and connections

docs.title: Step 4: Add the Navigator
docs.text:
Add node › Controller › Navigator. It is named sodero.navigator and uses the navigator settings of the same map bundle.

The navigator, using the same map bundle

docs.title: Step 5: Connect the Ports
docs.text:
Drag these five connections (from the required port on the left of a card to the provided port on the right of another):

From To sodero.localizer › camera sodero.camera_gateway.cam0 › camera sodero.localizer › odometry sodero.mlc.jackal › odometry sodero.navigator › localization sodero.localizer › localization sodero.navigator › map sodero.localizer › map sodero.navigator › mobile_base sodero.mlc.jackal › mobile_base The complete navigation graph, all nodes operating

While nodes run, the graph can show additional ports with a red dashed outline. Running nodes report them; they are not part of your saved graph and need no connection.

When the Station has several Strider nodes, make sure the localizer's odometry and the navigator's mobile_base connect to the same robot.

docs.title: Step 6: Start and Localize
docs.text:
1. In Isaac Sim, stop and play the scene so the Jackal is back at its starting pose.
  2. Start the nodes in order: sodero.localizer, then sodero.navigator (the gateway, the Strider and the camera already run).
  3. In the gateway's log, after Simulator connected again, open Strider and switch Twist and Servo On again (a simulation restart turns the servo off).
  4. Open Strider's Navigation page (the Strider link on the Navigator's card). Localization Status shows Healthy once the camera view matches the map.

If the status stays Initializing or Lost, or the robot is shown at the wrong place on the map, set the initial pose: click Set Initial Pose ①, press on the map where the robot is and drag in the direction it faces ②, then click Set initial pose (Relocalize here ③ when a pose was set before).

Setting the initial pose

docs.title: Step 7: Send a Goal
docs.text:
1. Click Set Goal, press on the map at the goal and drag in the direction the robot should face. Goal Pose shows the coordinates.

    The goal is set; the robot is localized (Healthy)

  2. Click Start Navigation. The planned path appears and the robot drives; Navigator shows following and Route Summary the remaining distance.

Following the path to the goal

When the robot arrives, Recent Goals shows Reached and Navigation Events Navigation idle: reached.

Goal reached The Jackal at the goal in Isaac Sim

docs.title: Step 8: Finish
docs.text: Click Cancel if a goal is still running, switch the servo off and choose Idle in Strider, then stop the nodes (navigator, localizer, camera, Strider, gateway) and the Isaac Sim scene.

docs.title: Camera Timing
docs.text:
Every camera frame carries its capture time on the Isaac Sim computer's clock, and the camera gateway accepts only frames captured at most 20 ms ahead of and 2 s behind Stellar X's clock. It drops the others: the Camera view in Step 2 stays empty, and the camera gateway's log shows Frames … are stale or carry capture times that do not match this Station's clock (clock skew?). Two computers that each follow a time server on the internet are easily more than 20 ms apart.

If you cannot synchronize the clocks, start Isaac Sim with RC_CAMERA_CAPTURE_TIME=0 as well. The frames then carry no capture time, and the camera gateway stamps each frame when it arrives. An arrival time is later than the capture time by the rendering and network delay, so synchronized clocks remain the better choice for localization.

LinuxWindows (Command Prompt) 
RC_CAMERA_CAPTURE_TIME=0 RC_ISAAC_CAMERA_DEVICES='[{"name": "cam0", "width": 320, "height": 240, "fps": 5}]' ./isaac-sim.sh

set "RC_CAMERA_CAPTURE_TIME=0"
set "RC_ISAAC_CAMERA_DEVICES=[{"name": "cam0", "width": 320, "height": 240, "fps": 5}]"
isaac-sim.bat

docs.title: Nodes After an Isaac Sim Restart
docs.text: Restarting Isaac Sim interrupts the nodes: the gateway loses the simulator, and the Strider's watchdog stops the robot. Once the scene plays again, restart them from the toolbar: Stop all nodes, then Start all nodes (Connect to Stellar Station › Stop, Pause and Play). The Localizer may still hold its last pose; set the initial pose again if the robot appears at the wrong place.

docs.title: Tips for Your Own Robot
docs.text:
• Run the simulation in real time. The controllers follow the simulation's time, but the camera localization runs on wall time. A slow simulation makes localization lag behind.
  • Skid-steer bases turn less than their wheels say, because the wheels slide sideways. Let the robot turn in place before it drives (rotate_to_heading_min_angle about 0.25 rad), and calibrate the wheel offsets of the .sddm so odometry matches the real turn.
  • Repeating structures (identical racks, long corridors) can mislead the localizer. Limit the correction per update (icp.max_jump_m, icp.max_jump_rad) and keep distinct objects in the camera's view.
  • The camera height in the map bundle's extrinsics is measured from the floor (Localization and Navigation).

docs.title: Working with AI Coding Agents
docs.text:
The SSH workspace is built for people and AI coding agents alike. Every sodero command prints JSON, every change is previewed before it is applied, and the workspace ships its own operating rules for agents. With an agent such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex, you describe a task in plain language and the agent runs the commands, reads the results and reports back:

  • "Which nodes are running, and why did the Strider node stop?"
  • "Add a camera gateway named cam0 and connect it to the localizer."
  • "Lower the navigator's top speed to 0.3 m/s."
  • "Write a module that drives the robot through these three waypoints."

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    You(["You"]) --> Agent["AI coding agent<br>on your computer"]
    Agent -- "ssh stellar-x 'sodero …'" --> WS["SSH workspace<br>on Stellar X"]
    WS -- "sodero CLI" --> Station["Stellar Station"]
    Station --> Nodes["Nodes:<br>gateways, controllers,<br>navigation, modules"]

The robot's workspace has no Internet access, and an AI agent needs the Internet to reach its language model. So the agent runs on your computer and works on the robot through SSH: it sends each command with ssh, reads the JSON that comes back and decides the next step.

The agent changes the robot only through sodero, which performs exactly the operations of the Station page. Whatever the agent builds, you can inspect and change on the Station page, and the other way round.

docs.title: 1. Prepare SSH Access
docs.text:
1. Register your computer's SSH key on the robot's Network Settings page.

  2. Add a host alias to ~/.ssh/config on your computer, so the agent can use a short name:

    Host stellar-x
    HostName 192.168.60.18
    Port 2222
    User sodero

  3. Check that a command runs without a prompt:

    ssh stellar-x sodero project status

    The first time, SSH asks you to confirm the robot's host key: answer yes. After that the command must run without any prompt. It prints one line of JSON that describes the robot's Station.

Tip (macOS · Linux): Reuse one SSH connection

Agents run many short commands. Reusing one SSH connection makes each call faster. Add these lines under Host stellar-x:

    ControlMaster auto
    ControlPath ~/.ssh/cm-%r@%h-%p
    ControlPersist 10m

docs.title: 2. Tell the Agent About the Robot
docs.text:
Create a working folder on your computer with an instructions file that your agent reads automatically when it starts: CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, AGENTS.md for Codex and most other agents. Copy this text into it:

# Stellar X robot

The robot's SSH workspace is reachable as `ssh stellar-x '<command>'`.

Before you change anything, read the robot's own rules and follow them:
`ssh stellar-x cat /workspace/AGENTS.md`

- Use the `sodero` CLI over SSH. It prints JSON; read `sodero --help` and
  `sodero capabilities` instead of guessing commands.
- Commands that change something only preview until `--execute` is added.
  Show me the preview and wait for my OK before you add `--execute`.
- Never move the real robot unless I ask for that motion.
- Keep source files on the robot under /workspace/my-work
  (create it with `mkdir -p /workspace/my-work` if it does not exist).

The robot's own rules (/workspace/AGENTS.md) tell the agent how to read results and exit codes, how to wait for long operations without polling loops, which nodes drive real hardware on this robot, and what it must never do. They are maintained with the robot's software, so you do not need to copy them.

These rules are instructions to the agent, not a safety function. An agent can misread them or make mistakes, and the sodero commands it runs have the same effect as your own clicks on the Station page. Approve every command that changes the robot yourself, and keep the robot's stop controls and the hardware emergency stop ready (Stop Controls).

docs.title: 3. Start the Agent
docs.text:
Claude CodeCodex CLIVS Code 
mkdir -p ~/stellar-x-work && cd ~/stellar-x-work
# save the text above as CLAUDE.md
claude

mkdir -p ~/stellar-x-work && cd ~/stellar-x-work
# save the text above as AGENTS.md
codex

Open the folder ~/stellar-x-work in VS Code and start your agent extension there (for example Claude Code or Codex). The agent runs on your computer and reaches the robot with ssh stellar-x.

Start with a read-only request to see that everything is connected:

Check the robot's Station and tell me which nodes exist and which are running.

The agent runs commands such as sodero topology get and sodero runtime status and summarizes the result.

docs.title: Example Tasks
docs.text: You ask What the agent does "Why did the Strider node fail?" sodero runtime status to find the failed node and its reason, then sodero runtime logs NODE "Add a camera gateway cam0 and connect it to the localizer." sodero topology get, then sodero topology add-node and sodero topology connect, each previewed first "Lower the navigator's maximum speed to 0.3 m/s." sodero navigation get --node sodero.navigator, edits the value, sodero navigation apply with the returned SHA-256 "Attach warehouse.nav to the localizer and the navigator." sodero navigation get --node sodero.localizer for its SHA-256, then sodero maps upload warehouse.nav --node sodero.localizer with it, previewed first (one upload serves both nodes) "Write a module that drives to these three points in a loop." Writes a package under /workspace/my-work, checks it, sodero packages upload, adds its node and starts it with sodero apps start "Drive the simulated robot forward 1 m." sodero tools call strider.set_mode, strider.servo_on, strider.set_twist and strider.stop on the simulated robot's target

docs.title: Stay in Control
docs.text:
• Review previews. Ask the agent to show the preview of every change. Nothing changes until a command runs with --execute.
  • Set approval rules in your agent. Most agents can require your approval before they run a command. A practical setup: allow read-only commands (status, get, list, logs) freely, and ask for approval for anything with --execute, tools call or apps call.
  • Real hardware moves. A robot tool called with --execute can move real equipment. Keep the area clear and keep the emergency stop within reach. The robot's rules tell the agent not to move the robot unless you ask for that motion, but only your approval of each command and the robot's own stop controls keep it from moving.

docs.title: Give the Agent the Documentation
docs.text:
• Inside the workspace, sodero-help prints every guide and /opt/sodero/docs/examples holds runnable examples. The robot's AGENTS.md points the agent to them.
  • This documentation is also published in a form made for language models: llms.txt (an index) and llms-full.txt (all pages in one file) at the root of each documentation version, for example https://docs.sodero.io/latest/llms-full.txt.

docs.title: SSH Workspace
docs.text:
Stellar X includes a development workspace that you reach over SSH. It runs on the controller itself, next to Stellar Station but separated from real-time control. It still shares the controller's memory and storage, so avoid very large builds while the robot is moving.

From the workspace you can:

  • inspect and change the Station with the sodero command-line tool: nodes, connections, design documents, settings, maps and packages;
  • read the status and logs of every node, as the Station page shows them, and call robot tools such as Strider, Motion Studio and navigation;
  • write and test your own programs and install them on the Station as modules;
  • let an AI coding agent do all of the above for you (see AI Coding Agents).

The workspace performs the same operations as the Station page: a node added with sodero topology add-node is the same node you would add with Add node.

docs.title: 1. Register Your SSH Key
docs.text:
The workspace accepts SSH keys only; there is no password sign-in. Register the public key of every computer that should connect, in the SSH ACCESS card of the robot's Network Settings page (http://ROBOT_ADDRESS:3000): copy the key command for your operating system, run it on your computer, paste the line it prints and click Add key. The steps and the commands are in Network Settings › SSH Access.

To revoke a computer's access, click the trash icon next to its key on the same page.

docs.title: 2. Connect
docs.text:
The SSH workspace card on the Network Settings page shows the command with a Copy button:

ssh -p 2222 sodero@192.168.60.18

Replace the address with your robot's address. The user name is always sodero and the port is always 2222.

Tip: Save a host alias

Add this to ~/.ssh/config on your computer, so that ssh stellar-x is enough:

Host stellar-x
    HostName 192.168.60.18
    Port 2222
    User sodero

Check where you are before you change anything:

sodero project status
sodero runtime status

Stellar X has a single Station, with the ID station. Every command uses it by default, so you never need --item.

docs.title: 3. What Is in the Workspace
docs.text:
Path Contents /workspace Your files. They stay on the robot across restarts and software updates. /workspace/README.md The workspace guide: terms, a five-minute start and the guide map /workspace/AGENTS.md Operating rules for AI coding agents (AI Coding Agents) /opt/sodero/docs/ All workspace guides and examples, read-only. Also linked as /workspace/docs. Tool Purpose sodero Station command-line tool (sodero CLI) sodero-help Prints the guides: sodero-help lists them, sodero-help navigation opens one Python 3.12 With numpy, PyYAML, requests, aiohttp and onnxruntime git, gcc, make, scp, sftp Standard development tools

The robot's workspace has no Internet access. Copy the dependencies your code needs from your computer (for example as wheel files) with scp.

docs.title: 4. Copy Files
docs.text:
Use scp or any SFTP client with the same address, user and port:

# Once: create a folder for your work on the robot
ssh -p 2222 sodero@192.168.60.18 mkdir -p /workspace/my-work

# From your computer to the robot
scp -P 2222 my_robot.gw sodero@192.168.60.18:/workspace/my-work/

# From the robot to your computer
scp -P 2222 sodero@192.168.60.18:/workspace/my-work/result.json .

docs.title: 5. Use VS Code
docs.text:
VS Code's Remote - SSH extension connects with the same command.

  1. In VS Code settings, set remote.SSH.localServerDownload to always. The robot has no Internet access, so VS Code copies its server from your computer.
  2. Run Remote-SSH: Add New SSH Host... from the Command Palette and enter ssh -p 2222 sodero@192.168.60.18.
  3. Run Remote-SSH: Connect to Host..., choose the robot's address and open the folder /workspace.

The first connection copies the VS Code server (about 230 MB) and takes a minute or two. Later connections take seconds.

docs.title: 6. Rules of the Road
docs.text:
• Preview first. A sodero command that changes something only previews until you add --execute. Read the preview, then repeat the command with --execute.
  • The robot is real equipment. A command with --execute can start nodes or move the robot. Run it only when the surroundings are clear and someone who can stop the robot is present.
  • Stop a node before you change it. The Station refuses changes to a running node. Stop it, apply the change, start it again.

Where to go next:

Task Where Command reference and examples sodero CLI Let an AI agent work on the robot AI Coding Agents Load a whole design document (.gw, .sdd, .sddm, .sdda) Station page: Design Documents Write your own module Modules

docs.title: sodero CLI
docs.text:
sodero is the command-line tool of the SSH workspace. It performs the operations of the Station page (adding nodes, connecting ports, loading settings and maps, starting nodes, calling robot tools) and prints every result as JSON, so people, scripts and AI agents can all use it.

The CLI is its own best reference:

Command What it gives sodero --help All command groups sodero GROUP ACTION --help Every option of one command, with defaults sodero capabilities The full command list, exit codes and limits as JSON sodero tools list / sodero tools describe TOOL The robot tools of the running nodes and their input schemas sodero-help / sodero-help NAME The workspace guides, for example sodero-help navigation

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• JSON output. Each command prints one JSON result on stdout. Pipe it through python3 -m json.tool to read it comfortably. A failure prints one JSON error on stderr: {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "details": ...}}.
  • Preview first. A command that changes something only previews until you add --execute. Read the preview, then repeat the command with --execute.
  • Versions. Changes to the node graph take --if-version N, the expected_version from sodero topology get. Changes to settings and documents take --if-sha256 SHA256 from the matching get. Each saved change returns the next value. If someone changed the Station page in the meantime, the change is refused with a conflict (exit code 6): read again and retry.
  • One Station. On a robot, the only item is the Station station. --item defaults to it and can be left out.
  • Node IDs. A node's ID comes from its module, not from the --kind option of topology add-node: --kind camera --name cam0 creates sodero.camera_gateway.cam0. Strider, Motion Studio and Articulation nodes are sodero.mlc.<name>, sodero.mmc.<name> and sodero.amc.<name> (for example sodero.mlc.jackal); gateways and the other modules are sodero.<kind>.<name> (for example sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal). The localizer, navigator and visual odometry have fixed IDs: sodero.localizer, sodero.navigator, sodero.visual_odometry.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning What to do 0 Success For an accepted change, check the returned state 1 Other failure Read error.message and fix the cause 2 Invalid arguments Check --help 3 Authentication or permission Reconnect; ask the robot's operator 4 Service unavailable Check the state before you repeat a change 5 Timeout Check the state; run the printed resume command 6 Conflict Read the current version or SHA-256 again, then retry 7 Busy Retry after a pause 8 Limit exceeded Reduce the size or count

docs.title: Command Map
docs.text:
Group Actions Use project status Station and workspace information runtime status, logs, start, stop, node start, node stop Which nodes run, their logs; start and stop nodes topology catalog, get, add-node, connect, disconnect, remove-node, import Edit the node graph tools list, describe, call Robot tools: Strider, Motion Studio, navigation, localization, documents… navigation list, get, apply Settings of the camera, visual odometry, localizer and navigator maps upload, attach Attach .nav map bundles to the localizer and navigator locomotion, policies list, get, apply; upload Legged locomotion and IMU settings; your own ONNX walking policy articulations get, configure, upload Joints and actuators of Articulation nodes packages list, upload, remove Your own modules apps start, stop, status, logs, call Nodes of your own modules watch, camera watch; camera snapshot Sample readings for a few seconds; save a camera picture files upload Stage a file on the robot for documents.apply (kept for at most 6 hours) run, programs run; programs list, programs logs Run a program in the workspace and keep its output

Worlds, project items, the project Library and the official asset catalog belong to Sodero Cloud. On a robot these commands answer NOT_AVAILABLE_ON_DEVICE.

docs.title: Status and Logs
docs.text:
sodero runtime status                                    # every node: configured, running, its state
sodero runtime logs sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal --lines 100
sodero tools call strider.get_state --input '{"target":"sodero.mlc.jackal"}'

docs.title: Start and Stop Nodes
docs.text:
sodero runtime node start sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal --execute          # gateway first
sodero runtime node start sodero.mlc.jackal --execute # then its controller
sodero runtime node stop sodero.mlc.jackal --execute

sodero runtime start --execute --wait starts every saved node, like Start all nodes on the Station page.

Start all nodes includes nodes that drive real hardware. Start nodes one by one when the graph contains hardware you do not want to run.

docs.title: Edit the Node Graph
docs.text:
Stop the nodes you change first, as on the Station page; changes apply when they next start. Every graph change needs the current version. Read it, preview, then execute:

sodero topology get                                       # note "expected_version", e.g. 12
sodero topology add-node --kind camera --name cam0 --if-version 12              # preview
sodero topology add-node --kind camera --name cam0 --if-version 12 --execute    # returns version 13
sodero topology connect --source sodero.localizer.camera \
    --target sodero.camera_gateway.cam0.camera --if-version 13 --execute

sodero topology catalog lists the node kinds (gateway, strider, motion_studio, articulation, camera, imu, vo, localizer, navigator, legged_locomotion, legged_navigator, package) with their ports.

docs.title: Change Settings of Built-in Nodes
docs.text:
sodero navigation list
sodero navigation get --node sodero.navigator > navigator.json   # the editable config and its sha256
# save the "config" part to config.json and change the values you need, then:
sodero navigation apply --node sodero.navigator --config @config.json --if-sha256 SHA256            # preview
sodero navigation apply --node sodero.navigator --config @config.json --if-sha256 SHA256 --execute

Stop the node first; the new settings apply when it starts again. These are the same settings the Station page shows in the node's inspector.

docs.title: Attach a Map
docs.text:
sodero runtime node stop sodero.navigator --execute          # stop the nodes that use the map
sodero runtime node stop sodero.localizer --execute
sodero runtime node stop sodero.visual_odometry --execute    # if the Station has one
sodero navigation get --node sodero.localizer                # note "sha256"
sodero maps upload /workspace/maps/warehouse.nav --node sodero.localizer --if-sha256 SHA256            # preview: checks the bundle
sodero maps upload /workspace/maps/warehouse.nav --node sodero.localizer --if-sha256 SHA256 --execute  # attach it

The localizer and the navigator share one map bundle, so one upload serves both. Start the nodes again afterwards. See Load and Configure a Map and Localization and Navigation.

docs.title: Modules (Your Own Programs)
docs.text:
sodero packages upload /workspace/my-work/patrol.tar.gz --execute
sodero topology add-node --kind package --package customer.patrol --if-version N --execute   # name from package.yaml
sodero apps start NODE --execute
sodero apps logs NODE --lines 100

See Modules for the package format.

docs.title: Robot Tools
docs.text:
sodero tools list                                        # tools of the running nodes, with their targets
sodero tools describe localization.set_initial_pose      # input schema
sodero tools call localization.set_initial_pose --input '{"x": -1.6, "y": 2.4, "yaw": 0.0}'            # preview
sodero tools call localization.set_initial_pose --input '{"x": -1.6, "y": 2.4, "yaw": 0.0}' --execute

A tool that changes something or moves the robot acts only with --execute. Strider and Motion Studio tools need the exact target (from tools list) when the Station has more than one robot of that kind, for example {"mode": "TWIST", "target": "sodero.mlc.jackal"} for strider.set_mode.

docs.title: Readings and Pictures
docs.text:
sodero watch --probe sodero.mlc.jackal --hz 5 --seconds 5
sodero camera snapshot sodero.camera_gateway.cam0 --output frame.png

docs.title: Backup and Restore
docs.text:
The whole Station (its node graph, design documents, settings and Station data) can be saved to one .sdr file and loaded again on the same or another Stellar X. Use it to back up a working system, to copy a system to another robot, or to bring a Station built in Sodero Cloud onto a robot.

An .sdr file does not contain installed module packages. To restore a Station on another Stellar X, prepare that unit first (Load on Another Stellar X).

docs.title: 1. Export the Station
docs.text:
Click Export SDR in the Runtime toolbar. Pending edits are saved first, then the browser downloads a file named after the Station, for example stellar-x.sdr.

The file contains:

Part Contents Runtime graph All nodes and their connections Robot documents The .sdd, .sddm and .sdda documents of the controllers Station data Gateway documents (.gw), settings of sensor and navigation nodes, maps and other Station state

Installed module packages are not part of the file; they stay on the controller.

Tip: Export the Station before larger changes, such as importing a new document over a working one or loading another .sdr.

docs.title: 2. Load an .sdr File
docs.text:
1. Stop all nodes (Start all nodes menu › Stop all nodes).
  2. Click Load SDR, drop the file or click Choose file.
  3. Click Load and restart.
Loading an .sdr file

The Station replaces its graph, robot documents and Station data with the file's content and restarts. The page shows Restarting the Station with … and reloads when the Station is back, usually within a minute. The nodes are not started; start them when you need them.

  • Installed modules stay installed.
  • If the file cannot be loaded, the Station keeps its data and the dialog says why.
  • After a successful load there is no command to return to the previous Station. Export the Station before you load another .sdr if you may need it again.

Loading is refused while any node runs: Stop all nodes before loading a .sdr.

docs.title: Files That Cannot Be Loaded
docs.text: Message Cause This .sdr holds a simulation, not a Station. The file is a World (simulation) export. Open it in Sodero Cloud. This robot does not have enough free disk space to load this .sdr. The unpacked file is too large for the controller's storage.

docs.title: 3. Load on Another Stellar X
docs.text:
An .sdr file carries the Station, not the software of the unit. Before you load it on another Stellar X:

  1. Make sure that the other unit runs the same version of the Stellar software as the unit the file comes from.
  2. Install the module packages that the Station's nodes use, in the same versions, on the other unit's Modules page. Built-in modules come with the unit.
  3. Load the file as described in Load an .sdr File.
  4. Check each node before you start it: the simulator address (Sim host) and camera addresses, which belong to the original site, and on real hardware the EtherCAT wiring and the drives, which must match the gateway documents. Start the gateways first and test real hardware as on a new robot.

docs.title: Design Documents
docs.text:
Gateways and robot controllers are configured by design documents. You create them in Stellar Designer, load them into nodes on the Station, and edit them later directly from the node.

File Node Edited with .gw Actuator gateway Stellar Gateway Designer (Gateway Designer) .sdd Motion Studio Stellar Designer, manipulator editor (Manipulator) .sddm Strider Stellar Designer, mobile robot editor (Mobile Robot) .sdda Articulation Stellar Designer, articulation editor (Articulated Robot)

Cameras, IMUs, visual odometry, the localizer and the navigator have no design document. They have settings that you edit in the node's inspector (see Settings of Sensor and Navigation Nodes).

Every new gateway or controller node starts with an empty document of its type, so you can either import a finished file or build the document from scratch with Edit Stellar Designer (Edit Stellar Gateway Designer for gateways).

docs.title: 1. Import a Document
docs.text:
1. Stop the node if it is running.
  2. Select the node. In the inspector's DEFINITION section, click the upload icon (Import .gw, Import .sdd, Import .sddm or Import .sdda).
  3. On From your PC ①, drop the file or click Choose file. The chosen file appears ②; click Import ③.
Importing a gateway document

The DEFINITION section then shows the file name and imported just now.

An import replaces the whole document of the node. Export the Station first if you may need the previous version (Backup and Restore).

My Library, Workspace Library and Sodero Assets list files stored in Sodero Cloud. They need a Sodero account and Internet access. On a controller without Internet access, use From your PC.

docs.title: 2. Edit a Document in Stellar Designer
docs.text:
Click Edit Stellar Designer (controllers) or Edit Stellar Gateway Designer (gateways) in the DEFINITION section. Stellar Designer opens in a new browser tab with the node's document. The breadcrumb at the top shows the node and the file, for example sodero.mlc.jackal / jackal.sddm.

  • Stop the node before you edit its document. While the node runs, the Station refuses to save.
  • Your edits are saved back to the node automatically. In an Articulation document, click Save configuration.
  • The arrow at the left of the breadcrumb returns to the Station.

The editors are described in Stellar Designer and Gateway Designer.

docs.title: 3. Point a Simulation Gateway at Its Robot
docs.text:
A simulation gateway also needs to know which robot in Isaac Sim it drives and where Isaac Sim runs. Select the gateway and click Change in its TARGET section:

Robot name and simulator address of a simulation gateway No. Field Value 1 Robot name The name of the robot's articulation prim in the Isaac Sim scene, for example jackal for /World/jackal 2 Sim host The IP address of the computer that runs Isaac Sim 3 Done Saves both values. They take effect when the gateway starts next time.

The robot name must match exactly. The gateway finds its robot in Isaac Sim by name only. If the names differ, the gateway keeps waiting for the simulator and the robot never moves. See Simulation Gateway.

docs.title: 4. Settings of Sensor and Navigation Nodes
docs.text:
Camera gateways, IMU gateways, visual odometry, the localizer, the navigator and legged locomotion are configured with settings forms in their inspector, and on a full-page Settings view that opens from the node card.

  • Stop the node, change the values, then click Save settings. Reload discards unsaved changes.
  • The localizer and the navigator share their settings with the map bundle. They can be saved only while the localizer, the navigator and visual odometry are stopped.
  • The localizer's map is loaded with Upload .nav (Load and Configure a Map). The navigator uses the same bundle.

The same settings can be read and written from the SSH workspace with sodero navigation get and sodero navigation apply (sodero CLI).

docs.title: 5. Rules for Documents
docs.text:
• A Motion Studio, Strider or Articulation document names the gateway it drives and the gateway's actuator indices (zero-based). Connect the node's servo_link to that same gateway.
  • A simulation gateway document has hardware.type: simulation. Its robot name and simulator address are set on the node (section 3).
  • The gateway must have enough actuators: the controller document maps every actuator it uses to a joint or wheel, and the gateway must provide at least that many.
  • Connect one robot controller to a gateway. To drive one manipulator through several gateways, use + Gateway link on its Motion Studio node.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
A module is a program packaged to run on the Station as a node. The built-in modules (gateways, controllers, navigation) come with Stellar X. You can install your own modules to add robot behaviors, task logic or custom device interfaces; they run next to the built-in ones and use the same interfaces.

This page installs, updates and removes module packages. To build a package yourself, see Create Custom Modules.

docs.title: 1. The Modules Page
docs.text:
Click Modules in the left sidebar. The page lists the modules that the nodes of your system use.

Modules used in this system No. Item Description 1 Add custom module Installs a module package from your PC (Install a Module) 2 TYPE Gateway, Controller, Compound or Application 3 USED BY How many nodes of the graph use the module

The ⋯ menu of a row offers Module info and, for your own modules, Remove module.

docs.title: 2. Install a Module
docs.text:
1. Click Add custom module.
  2. Drop the package (.tar.gz) or click Choose file, then click Add module.
Installing a module package
  • Uploading a package with the same name replaces the installed version. Nodes that use it keep their connections; stop and start them to run the new version.
  • Built-in modules cannot be replaced.

docs.title: Add and Start the Module's Node
docs.text:
1. Click Add node and choose the type that the module declares: Gateway, Controller, Compound or Application (the role in its subsystem.yaml: gateway, component, compound or app). Your module appears in the list with the CUSTOM badge. The status module of Create Custom Modules, for example, is a component and appears under Controller.
  2. Connect its required ports, for example to a Strider's mobile_base or a Motion Studio's manipulator.
  3. Right-click the node and choose Start node, or use Start all nodes.

If the module has its own web UI, a link with the module's name appears on its node card while it runs. Its logs appear in the inspector's LOGS section.

docs.title: Remove a Module
docs.text: Stop and delete the nodes that use the module, then choose Remove module in the ⋯ menu of its row.

docs.title: Nodes and Connections
docs.text: A Station is a graph of nodes connected through ports. This page shows how to add nodes, connect them, and rename or delete them. See Key Concepts for what the node types mean.

docs.title: 1. Add a Node
docs.text:
1. Click Add node in the toolbar (or right-click the empty canvas).

  2. Choose a node type ①, select a module ② and click Next ③.

    Gateway › Actuator gateway

  3. Enter a node name ① and click Add node ②. You can rename the node later in the inspector.

    Naming the node

The new node appears on the canvas in the Planned state. It is saved with the graph, but nothing runs until you start it.

docs.title: Node Types and Modules
docs.text:
Type Module Node ID Typical use Gateway Actuator gateway sodero.actuator_gateway.NAME Motors and drives, real (EtherCAT) or simulated (Isaac Sim) IMU gateway sodero.imu_gateway.NAME IMU and foot-contact data Camera gateway sodero.camera_gateway.NAME An RGB-D camera Controller Motion Studio sodero.mmc.NAME Manipulators Strider sodero.mlc.NAME Wheeled mobile bases Articulation sodero.amc.NAME Articulated robots with direct joint control Legged locomotion rc.legged_locomotion.NAME Walking robots driven by a walking policy Localizer sodero.localizer Map-based localization (one per Station) Visual odometry sodero.visual_odometry Camera-based odometry (one per Station) Navigator sodero.navigator Path planning and goal following (one per Station) Compound Your compound modules Several robot units combined into one system Application Your application modules Robot behaviors and task logic

Legged locomotion and Visual odometry need preparation that this documentation does not cover step by step. Legged locomotion runs a walking policy made for your robot, whose joint names and order must match the robot's Articulation document. Visual odometry needs a calibrated camera, and an IMU for walking robots. This documentation describes their connections and settings; ask Sodero support before you use them on your robot.

Modules marked SODERO are built in. Modules you installed on the Modules page are marked CUSTOM and appear under the type they declare. Each type also lists a … subsystem entry (Empty draft subsystem): it adds an empty placeholder node with no program behind it, for sketching a system, and that node cannot be started.

Choosing a controller module: ① Controller ② Strider ③ Next (the list scrolls)

Name rules. Gateway names are converted to lowercase. Controller names (Motion Studio, Strider, Articulation, Legged locomotion) start with a lowercase letter and use lowercase letters, digits and _, at most 20 characters. The Localizer, Visual odometry and Navigator have fixed names.

Tip: Give a robot's gateway and controller the same name, for example sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal and sodero.mlc.jackal. The graph stays easy to read, and Auto-connect finds the right partner.

docs.title: 2. The Node Card
docs.text:
A gateway and a Strider connected through servo_link Part Meaning Title and module The node ID and its module, for example sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal / Stellar actuator gateway. A running controller shows a link to its UI here. REQUIRES n/m Ports this node needs from other nodes: connected / total. Required ports sit on the left edge of the card. PROVIDES n/m Ports this node offers: ports with at least one connection / total. They sit on the right edge. Status The node's state, such as Planned, Operating or Error (Running Nodes).

The card border has the color of the node type: orange for gateways, blue-violet for controllers, purple for compounds and mint for applications.

docs.title: 3. Connect Ports
docs.text:
Connect a required port to a provided port of another node. There are three ways:

  • Drag from one port dot to another. While you drag, compatible ports pulse blue and incompatible ones turn red.
  • Click one port, then the other.
  • In the inspector of the node that requires the port, click Auto-connect next to the port. The Station picks the matching provider.

The Station accepts a connection only when the two ports are on different nodes, one requires and the other provides, and both use the same contract (the interface type shown under the port name in the inspector, for example api.actuator.servo.v1). It also enforces the system structure:

  • Only a controller may use a gateway.
  • An application uses controllers or compounds, never gateways directly.
  • An actuator gateway serves one robot controller (Motion Studio, Strider or Articulation) at a time.

docs.title: Common Connections
docs.text:
Node (requires) Port Connect to (provides) Motion Studio, Strider, Articulation servo_link Actuator gateway servo_link Legged locomotion servo, imu Articulation articulation, IMU gateway imu Localizer camera, odometry Camera gateway camera; Strider or Visual odometry odometry Visual odometry camera, imu (optional) Camera gateway camera; IMU gateway imu Navigator mobile_base, localization, map Strider mobile_base; Localizer localization and map

To remove a connection, select the node and click Disconnect next to the port in the inspector.

Tip: A Motion Studio node can drive actuators of several gateways. Click + Gateway link in its inspector to add another servo_link port.

docs.title: 4. The Inspector
docs.text:
Click a node to open its inspector. The sections depend on the node type.

A gateway node: ① Start node ② its document ③ import ④ Gateway Designer ⑤ TARGET ⑥ CONNECTION ⑦ LOGS A Strider node: ① Start node ② its controller UI ③ its document ④ Stellar Designer ⑤ import. The box shows the gateway it drives. Section Contents Header Node name (pencil icon to rename), module, state, and Start node / Stop node CONTROL Buttons that open the node's tool: Stellar Motion Studio, Strider, Articulation for controllers; Test Stellar Gateway for gateways. They unlock once the node runs. DEFINITION The node's design document: file name and when it was imported, Edit Stellar Designer / Edit Stellar Gateway Designer, and the upload icon to import a file (Design Documents) TARGET Simulation gateways only: the robot name in Isaac Sim and the simulator address (Simulation Gateway) Settings Camera, IMU, visual odometry, localizer, navigator and legged locomotion nodes: their settings form CONNECTION Requires and Provides ports with their contracts, Auto-connect and Disconnect LOGS Output and events of the node (Running Nodes)

docs.title: 5. Rename and Delete
docs.text:
• Rename: stop the node, then click the pencil icon next to the node name in the inspector.
  • Delete: stop the node, then right-click it and choose Delete node. The node and its connections are removed from the graph.
Right-click menu of a node Delete confirmation

Deleting a node cannot be undone. Export the Station first if you may need the node again (Backup and Restore).

docs.title: 6. Find Nodes in a Large Graph
docs.text:
• Filter shows nodes of one type or status.
  • Fit view zooms to show every node; Auto layout arranges the nodes by their connections.
  • The N issues chip at the left of the toolbar lists problems such as unconnected required ports; Locate jumps to the node.
Filter by node type and status

docs.title: Stellar Station Overview
docs.text:
Stellar Station is the control center of Stellar X. In a web browser you build the robot system as a graph of nodes (gateways, controllers, sensors, navigation and your own modules), load their design documents, start them, and watch their state and logs. The controller UIs (Motion Studio, Strider and Articulation) and Stellar Designer open from the Station as well.

Open the Station from any computer on the controller's network:

http://ROBOT_ADDRESS

In this guide the address is 192.168.60.18. On the controller's own network the Station needs no sign-in. Use a recent version of Chrome or Edge.

If you do not know the controller's address yet, see Network Settings.

docs.title: 1. Screen Layout
docs.text:
The Runtime page of Stellar Station No. Item Description 1 Runtime / Modules The two pages of the Station. Runtime is the node graph shown here; Modules lists the modules used in the system and installs your own (Modules). 2 LIVE and uptime The Station is running, and how long it has been running. 3 Save state Saved / Saving…. Every change to the graph is saved to the controller automatically. If a save fails, the label turns into Retry save. 4 Filter Shows only nodes of a type (Gateway, Controller, Compound, Application) or a status. Nodes connected to a match stay visible but dimmed. 5 Load SDR Replaces the whole Station with an .sdr file (Backup and Restore). 6 Export SDR Downloads the whole Station as an .sdr file. 7 Add node Adds a gateway, controller, compound or application node (Nodes and Connections). 8 Start all nodes Starts or stops every node in dependency order (Running Nodes). 9 Resources CPU, memory and GPU load of the controller. 10 Node card One node of the graph, with its ports and its state. 11 Canvas controls Zoom out, zoom level and zoom in, Fit view, Auto layout, and collapse or expand all node cards. Drag the empty canvas to move the view. 12 Inspector Details of the selected node: its state, controls, design document, connections and logs. The button at the right end of the toolbar shows or hides it.

Tip: Right-click the empty canvas to add a node directly, and right-click a node for its actions (start, stop, open its UI, delete).

docs.title: 2. Resources
docs.text:
Click Resources to see the controller's load. View details opens the system monitor.

Resource usage System monitor

The bars turn amber at 70 % and red at 85 %. Stellar X has no GPU, so GPU shows —.

docs.title: 3. Theme
docs.text: Click the Stellar mark at the top left and choose Theme › Midnight (dark) or Twilight (light).

docs.title: 4. What You Do on the Station
docs.text:
A typical robot system is built in this order. Each step has its own page.

    A["Add nodes<br>gateway + controller"] --> B["Load design documents<br>.gw · .sdd · .sddm · .sdda"]

docs.title: Running Nodes
docs.text:
Nodes run only when you start them. This page covers starting and stopping nodes, reading their state and logs, and opening the controller UIs.

Real hardware moves. Starting a gateway or controller that drives real motors can energize them. Before you start such nodes, make sure the robot's surroundings are clear and someone can reach the emergency stop (Stop Controls).

docs.title: 1. Start and Stop One Node
docs.text:
• Select the node and click Start node (or Stop node) in the inspector, or
  • right-click the node and choose Start node / Stop node.

Start a robot's nodes in dependency order: gateway first, then its controller, then nodes that use the controller (navigation, applications). Stop them in the reverse order.

A controller refuses to start until it has a document and its servo_link is connected:

  • Import a robot file (.sdd/.sddm/.sdda) first.
  • Connect servo_link to a gateway before starting it.

docs.title: 2. Start All Nodes
docs.text:
The Start all nodes button starts every node that is down, in dependency order: gateways → controllers → compounds → applications. Its menu also offers Stop all nodes, which stops consumers first.

The run menu
  • While a run is in progress, a banner shows the progress, and the menu offers Cancel. Nodes already started stay up when you cancel.
  • The run continues even if you close the browser. The page shows its progress again when you reopen it.
  • The result appears as a banner, for example Runtime topology is up.

Start all nodes starts every node of the graph, including nodes that drive real hardware. When the graph contains hardware you do not want to run, start the nodes one by one.

After Stellar X restarts, the Station comes back with its saved graph, documents and settings, but no node is started. Start the nodes again when you need them.

docs.title: 3. Node States
docs.text:
The footer of each node card and the inspector header show the node's state.

State Meaning Planned Saved in the graph, not started yet Booting / Starting Starting up Waiting binding A required port has no connection yet Waiting target A connected node is not ready yet Ready Started and waiting to operate Operating Running normally Running The process is up Paused Paused Degraded Running with reduced performance Disconnected Heartbeat lost Fault The node reported a fault. The inspector and the node log show the reason. Error / Failed The node reported an error. The inspector shows the reason. Stopped The process ended

The dot next to the state is green for Ready, Running and Operating, yellow while waiting, red for errors and grey otherwise. Problems are also counted in the N issues chip of the toolbar.

docs.title: 4. Open the Controller UIs
docs.text:
When a node runs, its tools unlock, in the inspector's CONTROL section or as a link on the node card:

Node Button Opens Motion Studio Stellar Motion Studio Motion Studio for the manipulator Strider Strider Strider for the mobile base Articulation Articulation Articulation for joint control Navigator Strider link on the card Strider's Navigation page Camera gateway Camera view link on the card The camera image Actuator gateway Test Stellar Gateway The Test Console, which moves single actuators without a controller A running Motion Studio node: the CONTROL button is unlocked

Each UI opens in a new browser tab. You can keep several open, one per robot.

Test Stellar Gateway is for a gateway that no robot controller uses. Stop the robot controllers first: the Station does not open a test while a Motion Studio node runs, and starting a robot controller (Motion Studio, Strider or Articulation) ends every running test.

docs.title: 5. Logs
docs.text:
The LOGS section of the inspector shows the node's recent output. Choose the stream in the drop-down and click Refresh:

Stream Contents Gateway events Gateway status and problems, each with a hint about what to check (gateways and their controllers) Standard output / Standard error The program's output Node log The node's own log file Process log Start and stop of the process Gateway events of a simulation gateway

Tip: When a node fails, read Gateway events of its gateway first. Most start-up problems (no simulator, wrong robot name, no EtherCAT link, drive faults) are reported there with a hint.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom What to check A controller stays in Waiting binding Its servo_link (or another required port) is not connected A simulation gateway runs but the robot does not move The gateway's Robot name must equal the articulation prim name in Isaac Sim; Isaac Sim must be playing; the Sim host must be the Isaac Sim computer (Simulation Gateway) An EtherCAT gateway fails to start Cable to the first drive's IN port, drive power, number of drives (EtherCAT Gateway) Process stopped during topology startup A node stopped right after Start all nodes. Read its logs, fix the cause, then start again Changes to a document are refused Stop the node first. A gateway document is also refused while the gateway's test is open: click Stop test before you stop the gateway (Test Console).

docs.title: EtherCAT Mobile Base
docs.text:
Updated example pair (2026-10-27)

Download both the .gw and .sddm files from this page again if you have older copies. They use the current sodero.* node IDs; older screenshots may still show rc.*. See Compatibility and Downloads.

This tutorial drives a four-wheel skid-steer base with four EtherCAT servo drives from Stellar X. It is the Quick Start system on real motors: Strider still drives the base, and an EtherCAT gateway takes the place of the simulation gateway. You will:

  1. wire the four drives to Stellar X,
  2. add the gateway and Strider on Stellar Station and load their example documents,
  3. bring up the EtherCAT network,
  4. turn each wheel on its own from the gateway's test console, and
  5. jog the wheels with Strider.
flowchart TB
    B["Your browser<br>Stellar Station · Strider"]
    subgraph SX ["Stellar X"]
        S["Strider<br>sodero.mlc.base"] -- servo_link --> G["EtherCAT gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.wheels"]
    end
    subgraph EC ["EtherCAT line"]
        direction LR
        D1["Drive 1<br>front left"] --> D2["Drive 2<br>front right"] --> D3["Drive 3<br>rear left"] --> D4["Drive 4<br>rear right"]
    end
    B --> S
    G -- "EtherCAT Out" --> EC

Real motors move. Lift the base so that its wheels are off the ground until every wheel turns the right way. Wire the drives' safe torque off (STO) and an emergency stop, and keep the emergency stop within reach (Stop Controls).

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
You need Details Stellar X Powered on and reachable from your PC (Network Settings). In this guide its address is 192.168.60.18. Four servo drives EtherCAT drives with the CiA 402 profile and cyclic synchronous velocity (CSV). Their RxPDO must include Target velocity (0x60FF) (EtherCAT Gateway › What You Need). Motors One motor per wheel. The example uses motors with a rated torque of 2.2222 Nm, a peak torque of 6.6667 Nm, a maximum speed of 1,890 rpm and an encoder with 524,288 counts per turn, each behind a 7.75 : 1 gear. A four-wheel base The example base has wheels of 0.098 m radius at ±0.131 m front and back and ±0.188 m left and right of the base center. Example files wheels.gw (EtherCAT gateway with four drives) and base.sddm (Strider).

Your drives, motors and base are probably not the example's. Load the example files anyway and change the values in the Gateway Designer and Stellar Designer, as the steps below describe.

docs.title: Step 1: Wire the Drives
docs.text:
1. Plug Stellar X's EtherCAT Out port into the IN port of the front-left drive.
  2. Connect its OUT port to the IN port of the front-right drive, then on to the rear-left and the rear-right drive.
  3. Power the drives and release their STO and the emergency stop.

The cable order is the actuator order of the gateway, and the Strider document assigns the actuators to the wheels:

Drive on the cable Gateway actuator Wheel 1st 1 (index 0) fl, front left 2nd 2 (index 1) fr, front right 3rd 3 (index 2) rl, rear left 4th 4 (index 3) rr, rear right

Do not use a network switch. EtherCAT frames must pass through the drives in a line (EtherCAT Gateway › Wire the Drives).

docs.title: Step 2: Add the Gateway and Load wheels.gw
docs.text:
1. Open http://192.168.60.18 in your browser.
  2. Click Add node, choose Gateway › Actuator gateway and click Next. Name it wheels and click Add node (Quick Start › Step 1).
  3. Select sodero.actuator_gateway.wheels. In its inspector, click the upload icon in DEFINITION (Import .gw), choose wheels.gw on From your PC and click Import.

  4. Click Edit Stellar Gateway Designer to check the document.

    ① four actuators, one per drive in cable order ② the Motor tab of actuator 1

    The gateway has four actuators ①, one per drive. Every actuator has the same Motor tab ②:

    Field Example value Rated torque 2.2222 Nm Max torque 6.6667 Nm Max speed 1,890 rpm Resolution 524,288 PPR Encoder offset 0 pulse Gear ratio 7.75

    The EtherCAT tab of each actuator holds the drive's position on the cable (Idx 0 to 3), its label (drive_fl to drive_rr) and the PDO mapping: the six RxPDO and the six TxPDO objects listed in Process Data, including Target velocity (0x60FF).

  5. If your hardware differs, change it here: select your drive in the EtherCAT tab and enter your motor in the Motor tab of each actuator (EtherCAT Gateway › Create the Gateway Document).

  6. Open 02 Verification, click Verify and fix any errors. Then click the back arrow to return to the Station.

docs.title: Step 3: Add Strider and Connect It
docs.text:
1. Click Add node, choose Controller › Strider and click Next. Name it base and click Add node.
  2. Select sodero.mlc.base, click the upload icon in DEFINITION (Import .sddm), choose base.sddm and click Import.
  3. Connect the two nodes: drag from the Strider's servo_link to the gateway's servo_link, or click Auto-connect next to servo_link in the Strider's inspector.
① the gateway and Strider connected through servo_link ② the gateway's document ③ the gateway's log after a start

base.sddm describes the example base: a skid-steer chassis with four drive wheels, 0.098 m wheel radius and 17 kg. For your own base, select sodero.mlc.base, click Edit Stellar Designer and enter its dimensions and limits (Mobile Robot (.sddm)).

docs.title: Step 4: Start the Gateway
docs.text:
1. Select the gateway and click Start node. Wait until its state is Operating.

  2. In its LOGS (stream Gateway events) ③, check that all four drives answered and reached operation:

    Gateway sodero.actuator_gateway.wheels starting: EtherCAT, 4 actuator(s), 1.0 ms cycle.
EtherCAT: starting on network port 'eth0' (4 drive(s) expected).
EtherCAT: found drive 1 (…).
EtherCAT: found drive 2 (…).
EtherCAT: found drive 3 (…).
EtherCAT: found drive 4 (…).
EtherCAT ready: 4 drive(s) operational, 1.0 ms cycle.

    Each found drive line names the drive as the drive reports itself.

If the gateway stops before EtherCAT ready, its log says why: no cable link, a drive missing from the chain, a PDO mapping that does not match the drive, or a drive that refuses the configuration. See EtherCAT Gateway › Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Step 5: Test the Wheels with the Test Console
docs.text:
The gateway's test console moves single actuators without a controller. This step uses its velocity mode to check every wheel before Strider drives them.

  1. Select the gateway and click Test Stellar Gateway in its CONTROL section. The test console opens in a new browser tab.

    ① the test console, connected to the gateway's servo_link ② the gateway's test console buttons

    While the test runs, the console is a node of the graph, sodero.actuator_test.wheels ①, and the gateway's CONTROL section shows Open test console and Stop test ②. The node has a red dashed outline because it is not part of your saved graph. It goes away when the test ends; do not add it to the graph with Adopt running.

  2. In the console, check that the top bar shows Gateway Connected and that there is one card per actuator, A1 to A4. Card A1 is actuator 1, the first drive on the cable.

    ① EMERGENCY STOP ② Servo ON and Servo OFF ③ the drive mode of all actuators ④ the target velocity of actuator 1

  3. Under DRIVE MODE — APPLY TO ALL AXES ③, choose VELOCITY and click Apply.

  4. Click Servo ON ②. The indicator on every card changes from Disable to Enable. Check the gateway's log on the Station page for Servo ON: all 4 drive(s) enabled. The cards show the requested state; only this log line confirms that all four drives are enabled.
  5. On card A1, press and hold the dqa_d · Target Velocity slider ④ and drag it to the right, to about 60 deg/s. The wheel turns while you hold the mouse button and stops when you release it. Keep the console's tab open while a wheel turns (Test Console › End the Test).
  6. Do the same on cards A2, A3 and A4.

Each card must turn its own wheel (Step 1) forward, the way the base drives forward. At 60 deg/s a wheel needs 6 s for one turn.

What you see Cause and fix A different wheel turns The cable order does not match the wheel order. Rewire the drives in the order of Step 1. The wheel turns backward The motor is mounted the other way round. Invert its direction in the drive, for example with the drive's polarity parameter as a start-up SDO in the EtherCAT tab. Leave the influence factor in the Strider document at 1 (Mobile Robot › Actuator Mapping). One turn takes clearly more or less than 6 s Gear ratio or Resolution in the gateway is wrong. The gateway's log shows Servo ON failed (the cards can still show Enable) A drive does not enable: check its STO and enable inputs, the emergency stop and its main power. Then click Servo OFF and Servo ON.

To change the gateway document, for example a drive's polarity, end the test first: click Servo OFF in the console and Stop test in the gateway's CONTROL section, then Stop node on the gateway. Edit and save the document, start the gateway, and open the test again (Test Console › Change the Gateway Document).

When every wheel passes, click Servo OFF. Then click Stop test in the gateway's CONTROL section. Closing the console's tab does not end the test.

Open the test while no robot controller runs: the Station does not open a test while a Motion Studio node runs, and starting a robot controller (Motion Studio, Strider or Articulation) ends every running test. EMERGENCY STOP ① stops all drives of the gateway and switches their servo off; click it again to release it. It does not replace the hardware emergency stop (Stop Controls).

docs.title: Step 6: Jog the Wheels with Strider
docs.text:
1. Select the Strider and click Start node. The gateway's log shows Robot controller connected.
  2. In the Strider's inspector, click Strider in CONTROL and open the Drive page (Strider › Jog the Base).
  3. Under Drive Mode, click Twist. Under Servo / Safety, switch Servo On. The gateway's log shows Servo ON: all 4 drive(s) enabled.
  4. Set Linear Velocity Limit to a low value, such as 0.1 m/s.
  5. Press and hold Forward (W) for a moment. All four wheels turn forward.
  6. Press and hold Turn Left (A). The left wheels turn backward and the right wheels forward.

The wheels passed the test console, so a wrong wheel or direction here comes from the Strider document: its actuator mapping must assign actuators 1 to 4 to fl, fr, rl and rr, each with the influence factor 1 (Mobile Robot › Actuator Mapping). If the wheels turn too fast or too slow, check the wheel radius in the Strider document.

When every wheel turns the right way, switch the servo off and click Idle. Put the base on the ground and drive it slowly, with the limits still low.
